summary: Codemasters' touring-car series that expanded into Race Driver and then the Grid franchise, mixing licensed championships, story campaigns, track editors, and modern multi-discipline circuit racing.

emulation.notes: Use PC for the main route.

primary.why: The first TOCA game was released for PlayStation and Windows, with a later Game Boy Color port. Windows offers the highest output ceiling and LAN support, while Game Boy Color is a separate low-fidelity adaptation.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release on period hardware or a compatibility setup; use PlayStation emulation as a fallback.

primary.why: TOCA 2 was released for PlayStation and Windows. Windows is the best-fidelity route and includes PC skin-import support; no PlayStation-exclusive content is sourced.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release on period hardware or a compatibility setup.

emulation.notes: Use PlayStation emulation for the primary route.

primary.why: TOCA World Touring Cars was released for PlayStation and Game Boy Advance, with no Windows version. The PlayStation release is the full main version; the GBA version is a handheld adaptation.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation version on original hardware or DuckStation.

entries.title: TOCA Race Driver

primary.why: TOCA Race Driver released on PlayStation 2, Windows, and Xbox. Windows is the highest-fidelity route; the later Xbox Live support is notable but not required content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release on a compatibility setup; use Xbox with Insignia/XLink Kai only for online-preservation interest.

entries.remaster_caveats: Regional titles include DTM Race Driver, Pro Race Driver, and V8 Supercars: Race Driver.

entries.title: TOCA Race Driver 2
entries.definitive_edition: Windows release plus PS2 Catalunya side route

emulation.notes: Use PC for the main route and PCSX2 for the PS2-exclusive track.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC output with PS2 secondary content

primary.why: TOCA Race Driver 2 released on Xbox, Windows, PlayStation 2, mobile, and PSP. Windows is the highest-fidelity route, but the PS2 version has a sourced additional Catalunya track, so it is marked as a secondary content route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release for the main career; sample the PlayStation 2 version for the extra Catalunya track if preserving all content.

secondary.exclusive_content: Additional Catalunya track in the PlayStation 2 version.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the Catalunya track on PS2/PCSX2 after completing the Windows route.
secondary.why: The Windows release is best for fidelity, but the PS2 version has a sourced extra track.

entries.remaster_caveats: Regional titles include DTM Race Driver 2 and V8 Supercars Australia 2; US PSP release is Race Driver 2006.

entries.title: TOCA Race Driver 3

primary.why: TOCA Race Driver 3 released on Windows, PlayStation 2, Xbox, PSP, and OS X. Windows is the highest-fidelity route and later had a GOG-compatible release; no platform-exclusive content is sourced.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows/GOG release if available; use console or Mac ports only as fallbacks.

entries.remaster_caveats: Last entry using the TOCA title before the series branding shifted toward Race Driver/Grid.

emulation.notes: Use DS hardware for native touch interaction if preferred.

primary.why: Race Driver: Create & Race was developed exclusively for Nintendo DS and added a track editor to the handheld TOCA/Race Driver line. DS is the only sourced platform.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Nintendo DS hardware or melonDS/DeSmuME with touch controls configured.

entries.title: Race Driver: Grid
entries.definitive_edition: Windows release plus optional DS editor side route

emulation.emulator: Native PC / RPCS3 / Xenia / melonDS / arcade preservation
emulation.notes: Use PC for the main game and DS emulation/hardware for the editor side route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC output with DS secondary content

primary.why: Race Driver: Grid released on Windows, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, Nintendo DS, arcade, OS X, and Java ME. Windows is the high-fidelity main route, while the DS version has a sourced track designer/customization feature worth a secondary side route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release for the main game; sample the DS version for track-designer content if desired.

secondary.exclusive_content: DS-specific track designer/custom circuits and handheld customization implementation.
secondary.what_to_play: Try the DS track designer and a few custom circuits separately.
secondary.why: The PC release is highest fidelity, but the DS version has a sourced editor feature not present in the same way on PC.

entries.title: Grid 2

primary.why: Grid 2 released on Windows, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, and later OS X Reloaded Edition. Windows is the highest-fidelity route, but online servers were shut down on March 16, 2026.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release offline or with any still-working preservation/community options; expect official online services to be unavailable.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster is sourced; online services are shut down.

entries.title: Grid Autosport
entries.definitive_edition: Windows release / Black Edition where owned

emulation.notes: No emulation needed for the recommended route.

primary.version: PC release / Black Edition where owned
primary.why: Grid Autosport released on Windows, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, Linux, OS X, iOS, Nintendo Switch, and Android. Windows has the highest fidelity ceiling and the Black Edition route where owned; later Switch/mobile ports are strong portable options but not content-superior.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with owned DLC/Black Edition content; use Switch/mobile for portable play.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster is sourced; online services are shut down.

entries.title: Grid

emulation.notes: No emulation needed for the recommended route.

primary.why: Grid 2019 released on Windows, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Stadia, and Amazon Luna. Windows is the highest-fidelity route, but the game was delisted in November 2023 and online services shut down on December 19, 2025.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release if already owned; expect official online services to be unavailable.

entries.remaster_caveats: Delisted in November 2023; online services shut down on December 19, 2025.

entries.title: Grid Legends

emulation.notes: No emulation needed for the recommended route.

primary.version: PC release with DLC where owned
primary.why: Grid Legends released on Windows, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S, Meta Quest, macOS, iOS, Android, and Nintendo Switch 2. Windows has the highest fidelity ceiling and complete DLC route; Meta Quest is a VR side platform but not a content-superior main route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with current updates and owned DLC; use Quest only if specifically preserving the VR version.

entries.remaster_caveats: Later ports add platform reach rather than a definitive remaster.
